- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions to avoid excessive overshoot.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and forecast is rising, model frequently overestimates; apply a 1–3% downward adjustment to avoid mean reversion bias.
- In early forecast windows (e.g., 30d), model often misses mean reversion; if true outcome shows strong pullback after peak, reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 7–14 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.8), model tends to lag true price movements; adjust forecast to align with 1–2 day lag in sentiment-driven trends.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., high → low → high), model overreacts; dampen forecast volatility by 10–20% in subsequent periods.
